title: Chicken and Chili Soup
imagePrompt: A deep bowl of ivory-gold, silky-smooth broth cradles a mound of shredded chicken, its threads pale and tender, studded with chopped serrano chilies and pinto beans peeking through the surface. Steam rises where the soup is ladled over a scoop of white rice, the broth soaking into the grains at the edges. Bright flecks of chopped cilantro and a swirl of sour cream sit on top, the cream just beginning to melt into the hot broth in streaks.
subtitle: A whole chicken simmered with garlic, onion, and serranos into a silky blended broth with shredded chicken, pinto beans, and lime.

ingredients.heading: Ingredients
ingredients.note: The broth gets blended smooth, then built back up with shredded chicken, blistered serranos, and beans.
items: 1 whole chicken (4–5 lbs)
6 bay leaves
10 cloves fresh garlic
1 whole onion, cut in half
4–5 serrano chilies
1 tsp chili powder
2 tsp dried oregano
1 tbsp sea salt
1 tbsp freshly cracked black pepper
4 cups chicken stock
Water, just enough to cover the chicken
Juice of 1 lime
1 can pinto beans, drained
Cooked rice, for serving
Fresh cilantro, for serving
Sour cream, for serving
ingredients.callout: Key rule: Blend the cooked onion and garlic straight into the broth—no chunks. The serranos get chopped and stirred back in separately for real heat and texture.

body.html: A whole chicken simmers low and slow with garlic, onion, and serranos until it falls off the bone. The broth gets strained and blended silky-smooth, then built back up with shredded chicken, chopped chilies, and pinto beans.

items: Mise en place — rinse the chicken, peel garlic, halve the onion, and measure the seasonings
Simmer the chicken low and slow until it pulls apart
Strain + blend the broth with the cooked onion and garlic until smooth
Shred the chicken and prep the serranos
Finish with lime, chopped serranos, and pinto beans
Serve over rice with cilantro and sour cream

body.html: Lesson learned: Keep the cooked serranos out of the blender—chop and stir them back in whole for real heat and texture, not just background spice.

items: Rinse the whole chicken and pat dry.
Peel the 10 cloves garlic and cut the onion in half.
Rinse the 4–5 serrano chilies whole—they go in uncut.
Measure the chili powder, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Measure 4 cups chicken stock and have water ready to top off the pot.
Juice the lime and drain the can of pinto beans.
Gather a large stockpot, immersion blender, strainer, and tongs.

body.html: Immersion blender ready: Keep it within reach for later—you'll blend the broth right in the pot.

slides.title: Simmer the Chicken
slides.checkboxLabel: Simmer covered ~1½ hours until falling apart

items: Add the chicken, bay leaves, garlic, onion, serranos, chili powder, oregano, salt, and pepper to a large pot.
Pour in the 4 cups chicken stock, then add just enough water to cover the chicken.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low.
Cover and gently simmer for about 1½ hours, until the chicken is very tender and pulls easily from the bone.

body.html: Doneness cue: The chicken should shred with almost no resistance—if it's still clinging to the bone, keep simmering.

slides.title: Strain + Blend the Broth
slides.checkboxLabel: Strain broth, blend onion + garlic until smooth

items: Remove the chicken to a plate or tray to cool slightly.
Strain the stock, discarding the bay leaves and any loose bones.
Set the cooked serrano chilies aside—don't discard them.
Reserve the cooked onion and garlic and return them to the pot with the strained broth.
Use an immersion blender to blend the broth until completely smooth.

body.html: Why blend: The soft-cooked onion and garlic thicken the broth just enough to give it body—no flour or cream needed.

slides.title: Shred Chicken + Prep Serranos
slides.checkboxLabel: Shred chicken, deseed and chop serranos

items: Remove all the meat from the chicken and shred it.
Return the shredded chicken to the blended broth.
Deseed the reserved serrano chilies and coarsely chop them.

body.html: Adjust the heat here: Keep the seeds and ribs in a chili or two for more spice, or discard all of them for a milder soup.

slides.title: Finish + Simmer
slides.checkboxLabel: Add lime, serranos, and beans; simmer 5 min

items: Add the lime juice, chopped serranos, and drained pinto beans to the pot.
Taste and adjust salt as needed.
Simmer for another 5 minutes to let the beans heat through and the flavors settle.

slides.title: Serve
slides.checkboxLabel: Serve over rice with cilantro and sour cream

items: Spoon the soup over cooked rice in each bowl.
Finish with fresh cilantro and a dollop of sour cream.

body.html: Serving tip: Add the rice to the bowl first, then ladle the soup over so it soaks up the broth without going mushy in the pot.
